overview: CMOC Group Limited (formerly China Molybdenum, dual-listed as 603993.SH on the Shanghai Stock Exchange and 3993.HK on HKEX) is a Chinese-controlled, globally diversified mining and metals-trading group. Its core assets are the Tenke Fungurume (TFM, ~80%-owned) and Kisanfu (KFM, ~71.25%-owned) copper-cobalt mines in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) — now respectively a top-5 global copper mine and the world's largest cobalt mine — alongside molybdenum/tungsten mines at Luanchuan (Henan, China), niobium and phosphate fertilizer operations in Brazil (Catalão), a growing gold portfolio (Brazil, the Ecuador Cangrejos project via the 2025 Lumina Gold acquisition), and the Geneva-based IXM base-metals trading subsidiary, one of the world's top-three metal traders. It is controlled by Cathay Fortune Corporation (CFC) and is the world's largest cobalt producer and a top-5 global copper producer.

business_model.summary: A 'mining + trading' dual-engine model: the mining segment covers the full value chain (exploration-mining-beneficiation-smelting) across copper, cobalt, molybdenum, tungsten, niobium, phosphate fertilizer and (since 2025) gold, while the trading segment (IXM) markets the Group's own output plus third-party base metals through an 80+-country network, generating trading margin and market intelligence that feeds back into M&A and production-pacing decisions. Mining-segment revenue in FY2025: copper RMB55.1bn, cobalt RMB6.2bn, molybdenum RMB6.3bn, tungsten RMB2.4bn, niobium RMB3.6bn, phosphate contributing to a combined niobium/phosphate RMB7.7bn. Overall FY2025 group operating revenue was RMB206.7bn (-3.0% YoY, largely IXM trading volume/price effects), while net profit attributable to shareholders surged 50.3% YoY to RMB20.3bn on higher copper/cobalt prices and volumes. H1 2026 revenue reached RMB135.3bn (+42.8% YoY) with net profit of RMB16.2bn (+86.3% YoY), reflecting the cobalt price spike from DRC export restrictions and continued copper volume growth.

revenue_streams.name: Trading (IXM)
revenue_streams.description: Geneva-based base-metals trading arm; large revenue contributor on a gross basis but low-margin pass-through volume; majority of consolidated group revenue by value though a small share of profit.

revenue_streams.name: Copper (mining segment)
revenue_streams.description: FY2025 copper segment revenue RMB55.1bn (+31.6% YoY) on 741.1kt production (+14% YoY), gross margin 55.2%. TFM and KFM are the key assets; capacity being expanded toward 1mt by 2028.

revenue_streams.name: Cobalt
revenue_streams.description: FY2025 cobalt segment revenue RMB6.2bn (-29.4% YoY on export-quota-constrained sales volume despite record 117.5kt production), gross margin jumped to 63.6% as prices spiked on DRC export restrictions. H1 2026 cobalt pricing and sales rebounded sharply.

revenue_streams.name: Molybdenum & Tungsten
revenue_streams.description: Luanchuan (Sandaozhuang/Shangfanggou) operations in China; FY2025 combined revenue ~RMB8.8bn, consistent high-margin base business.

revenue_streams.name: Niobium & Phosphate (Brazil)
revenue_streams.description: World's #2 niobium producer and a leading Brazilian phosphate fertilizer producer; FY2025 mining-sector revenue RMB7.7bn, niobium gross margin 44.4%.

revenue_streams.name: Gold (new segment)
revenue_streams.description: Entered gold in 2025 via acquisitions of Odin Mining (Ecuador, including the large Cangrejos deposit via the Lumina Gold deal, ~US$420-580m) and four Brazilian gold mines (Aurizona, RDM, Fazenda, Santa Luz), establishing a 'Copper-Gold Dual Core' strategic pillar; management targets 20+ tonnes of annual gold production capacity.

business_model.customer_type: B2B — global industrial and institutional customers: battery/EV supply chain and specialty chemical makers (cobalt), copper smelters/fabricators and industrial users (copper, via IXM and direct sales), steel and superalloy producers (molybdenum/tungsten), steel and aerospace alloy makers (niobium), agricultural distributors (phosphate fertilizer in Brazil), and global commodity trading counterparties via IXM.
business_model.geographic_mix: Mining operations concentrated in the DRC (copper/cobalt, the largest profit contributor), China (molybdenum/tungsten, Henan), Brazil (niobium, phosphate, gold) and Ecuador (gold, development stage). Trading (IXM) spans over 80 countries across Asia, Europe, the Americas. Revenue/earnings are heavily weighted to the DRC copper-cobalt complex; corporate management is dual-headquartered in Shanghai and Hong Kong, with listings on both SSE and HKEX.

main_competitors: BHP, Rio Tinto, Southern Copper (global copper majors)
Trafigura, Glencore, Mercuria (metals trading, competing with IXM)
competitive_position.market_position: World's largest cobalt producer (TFM + KFM account for the majority of global mined cobalt supply) and a top-5 global copper producer; world's #2 niobium producer; a leading Brazilian phosphate fertilizer producer; and one of the world's top-three base-metal traders via IXM. Ranked 12th in the Mining.com Top 50 and 135th in the 2025 Fortune China 500.

moat_factors.description: TFM and KFM are among the highest-grade, lowest-cost copper-cobalt orebodies globally; management explicitly attributes 60% of its cost advantage to 'resource endowment' secured through contrarian, cycle-bottom M&A (TFM acquired 2016, KFM 2020).

As the dominant global cobalt supplier with low by-product costs (cobalt recovered alongside copper), CMOC can profitably run at full production even at depressed cobalt prices, a structural advantage over higher-cost, cobalt-only producers.

Owning a top-3 global metals trader gives CMOC proprietary market intelligence, sales-pacing flexibility, and marketing reach that most pure-play miners lack, though it also dilutes consolidated margins (high-revenue, low-margin trading volume).

Track record of large contrarian acquisitions at cycle lows (TFM, KFM, and now Lumina Gold/Ecuador and Brazilian gold assets) under a stated 'multi-commodity, multi-country, multi-stage' strategy, diversifying into gold as a hedge/second core alongside copper.

Backing from controlling shareholder Cathay Fortune Corporation and broader Chinese industrial-policy support for securing critical minerals supply chains (cobalt, copper for EVs/batteries) provides capital access and strategic priority, though it is also a governance/geopolitical risk factor (see below).

weaknesses: Extreme geographic concentration of profit in one country (DRC) with elevated political, regulatory and expropriation/royalty risk
Limited pricing power — commodity producer selling into globally-set copper/cobalt/molybdenum prices with no brand differentiation
Trading segment (IXM) has structurally low margins and dilutes consolidated profitability optics despite generating the bulk of headline revenue
Export-quota exposure makes reported cobalt sales volume and revenue highly unpredictable year to year, independent of the company's own production execution
History of regulatory conflict with the DRC state (Gécamines royalty dispute, export bans) signals ongoing host-government renegotiation risk even after settlements

growth_drivers: TFM and KFM copper capacity expansion: KFM Phase II progressing, expected to add ~100kt/yr copper capacity; TFM Phase III targeted to help the Group reach ~1 million tonnes annual copper production by 2028, roughly doubling current DRC copper output
2026 copper production guidance of 760,000-820,000 tonnes (up to +11% YoY) following 2025 output of 741.1kt (118% of guidance midpoint)

Cobalt price normalization/upside as DRC export quotas (31,200 tonnes allocated to CMOC for 2026, part of a combined 87,000-96,600 tonne national quota for 2026-2027) constrain supply growth industry-wide while CMOC remains the largest quota holder and lowest-cost producer, able to profit from both price appreciation and relative market share retention

New gold pillar ('Copper-Gold Dual Core' strategy): Lumina Gold/Cangrejos project in Ecuador (large, long-life, low-cost primary gold-copper deposit) plus four Brazilian gold mines (Aurizona, RDM, Fazenda, Santa Luz), targeting 20+ tonnes/yr gold production capacity and management commentary (Jefferies) that gold could contribute >10% of group gross profit by 2030
Continued M&A optionality under the 'multi-commodity, multi-country, multi-stage' strategy, with management signaling further expansion in Africa, South America and Asia

By-product credit economics: cobalt is recovered as a by-product of copper mining at TFM/KFM, giving CMOC a structurally lower all-in cost per pound of copper (and vice versa) than single-metal peers, supporting margin resilience through commodity cycles

Secular demand tailwinds: copper demand from electrification, grid build-out and AI/data-center power infrastructure; cobalt demand from EV battery cathode chemistries (even as nickel-manganese-cobalt mix shifts evolve)

business.description: The large majority of group profit comes from TFM and KFM in the DRC, exposing CMOC to that country's political instability, infrastructure constraints (power, logistics), community relations and historically adversarial state-owned-enterprise relationships (Gécamines).

business.risk: Cobalt price volatility and oversupply risk
business.description: Cobalt prices swung from near nine-year lows in 2024 to a post-2022 high above US$56,000/tonne by early 2026 purely on DRC export-policy shifts (ban then quota), not demand fundamentals; a quota loosening, demand substitution (lower-cobalt battery chemistries), or resumed oversupply could sharply reverse gains.

CMOC's 2026 DRC cobalt export allocation (31,200 tonnes) is roughly 27% of its 2025 Congolese cobalt output, with 'use-it-or-lose-it' rules (unused quota forfeited to a strategic reserve) and a regulator (ARECOMS) that can adjust quotas based on market conditions — creating a structural mismatch between production capability and sellable/exportable volume.

The 2025 entry into gold (Lumina Gold/Cangrejos, Brazilian mines) is a new, unproven business line requiring large development capex (Cangrejos pre-feasibility capex estimated at ~US$925m) with integration and permitting risk, particularly in Ecuador.
IXM contributes the majority of consolidated revenue at thin margins, so headline revenue trends can diverge materially from underlying mining-segment profitability and can obscure analysis.

financial.description: Gearing ratio was 50.3% at end-FY2025 (up 0.8pp YoY) after heavy capex on TFM/KFM expansions and the Lumina Gold and Brazilian gold acquisitions; operating cash flow fell 35.6% YoY in FY2025 despite higher profit, reflecting working-capital and investment demands.

Revenue is predominantly USD-linked commodity sales while costs are a mix of RMB (China operations), USD, Congolese franc and Brazilian real, creating multi-currency translation and transaction exposure.

Doubling DRC copper capacity to ~1mt by 2028 (TFM Phase III, KFM Phase II) plus new gold-mine development implies a sustained heavy capex program that could strain free cash flow if commodity prices soften.

regulatory.description: The DRC government's cobalt export ban (Feb-Oct 2025) and subsequent quota system (administered by ARECOMS, the DRC's strategic minerals regulator) directly caps CMOC's exportable cobalt volume through at least 2027, with discretionary government authority to adjust allocations.

CMOC settled an $800m dispute with Gécamines (the DRC state miner) in 2023 over alleged royalty underpayment at TFM, agreeing to pay the sum through 2028 plus minimum cumulative dividends of $1.2bn to Gécamines and expanded Gécamines subcontracting/offtake rights — illustrating ongoing fiscal-term renegotiation risk in the DRC's evolving mining code environment.

As a Chinese-controlled company dominant in cobalt (a critical mineral for EV batteries and defense-adjacent supply chains), CMOC faces potential scrutiny or restrictive policy action from Western governments seeking to de-risk critical-mineral supply chains away from Chinese-controlled DRC output.
Simultaneous compliance with CSRC/SSE and HKEX/SFC disclosure regimes, and periodic divergence in A-share vs H-share investor bases/valuations, adds governance and reporting complexity.

macro.description: Copper is CMOC's single largest segment by revenue and profit; a global growth slowdown, China property-sector weakness, or a reversal of the AI/electrification capex cycle could materially pressure prices and group earnings.
Battery chemistry shifts toward lower-cobalt or cobalt-free (LFP, high-nickel) cathodes in EVs could structurally dampen long-term cobalt demand growth, independent of near-term DRC supply dynamics.
Molybdenum/tungsten demand (steel, superalloys) and broader group sentiment are linked to Chinese industrial activity and property/infrastructure cycles.

macro.risk: DRC/Central Africa political and security risk
macro.description: Broader regional instability (eastern DRC conflict dynamics, though TFM/KFM are in the south, Katanga region) and infrastructure (power supply, logistics corridors) bottlenecks remain a persistent operating risk across DRC mining generally.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Copper fundamentals are viewed as structurally favorable medium-term given electrification, grid investment and AI/data-center power demand, with many forecasters expecting tightening concentrate supply. Cobalt is in a policy-driven supply squeeze: DRC export quotas (set at roughly 87,000-96,600 tonnes/year combined for 2026-2027, versus a much larger underlying production base) are expected to keep the market tight-to-deficit through 2026-2027, supporting prices after the 2023-2024 glut. Gold has become a strategic second pillar for diversified miners amid geopolitical and macro uncertainty, which CMOC is now pursuing directly.
macro_factors.cyclicality: High. CMOC is a leveraged play on copper and cobalt prices, both of which are cyclical and, in cobalt's case, additionally subject to discontinuous regulatory supply shocks (bans/quotas) rather than smooth market cycles.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate — capex-heavy mine expansion projects (TFM Phase III, KFM Phase II, Cangrejos development) are sensitive to financing costs, and commodity prices broadly carry an inverse relationship with real rates/USD strength.
key_input_costs: Energy/power (DRC grid constraints, diesel for backup power)

recent_developments.event: Agreed to acquire Lumina Gold Corp (TSXV) for approximately C$581m (~US$420m), securing the large Cangrejos gold-copper deposit in Ecuador; deal closed 24 June 2025, central to the new 'Copper-Gold Dual Core' strategy.

Completed acquisition of Odin Mining Corp and four Brazilian gold mines (Aurizona, RDM, Fazenda, Santa Luz, Bahia Complex), establishing CMOC as a new entrant in global gold production alongside its existing metals.

DRC government imposed a nationwide cobalt export ban (Feb 2025), later replaced by a formal export quota system (from mid-October 2025) administered by strategic minerals regulator ARECOMS, fundamentally resetting the global cobalt supply/price landscape.

CMOC issued 2026 production guidance: copper 760,000-820,000 tonnes (+up to 11% YoY) and cobalt maintained at 100,000-120,000 tonnes, following record 2025 output of 741.1kt copper and 117.5kt cobalt (both well above original guidance).

CMOC's 2026 DRC cobalt export quota allocation confirmed at 31,200 tonnes (about 27% of 2025 Congolese cobalt output), with use-it-or-lose-it forfeiture rules; company stated at its April 2026 AGM that maintaining normal (full) production remains the optimal strategy given low by-product costs even with constrained exportable volume.

FY2025 annual report (released ~31 March 2026) showed record results for a 5th consecutive year: revenue RMB206.7bn (-3.0% YoY), net profit attributable to shareholders RMB20.3bn (+50.3% YoY), ROE 26.61% (+5.65pp), driven by sharply higher copper (+31.6% revenue) and cobalt (gross margin +29.3pp to 63.6%) profitability even as cobalt sales volume/revenue were constrained by export curbs.

Positive profit alert and H1 2026 interim results (announced ~19 August 2026): revenue RMB135.3bn (+42.8% YoY), net profit attributable to owners RMB16.15bn (+86.3% YoY), operating cash flow RMB16.33bn (+36.0% YoY); copper production 388.0kt (+9.7% YoY) at 62.88% gross margin; interim dividend of RMB0.95 per 10 shares declared.

Sell-side sentiment stayed broadly bullish: Bank of America reiterated Buy (HK$28 target in April 2026, trimmed to HK$22 by July 2026), Jefferies initiated Buy (HK$25.9 H-share target, Jan 2026) citing gold could reach >10% of group gross profit by 2030, Citigroup raised its target to HK$28.3; A-share consensus (StockAnalysis/S&P Global, mid-2026) was 'Strong Buy' with an average target near RMB25.4.

Continuing payments under the 2023 $800m Gécamines royalty-dispute settlement (payable through 2028) and minimum cumulative TFM dividends of $1.2bn to Gécamines remain an ongoing cash obligation and reminder of DRC fiscal-renegotiation risk.

guidance.as_of: 2026 production guidance filing (January 2026) and H1 2026 interim report (19 August 2026)

items.notes: Up to +11% YoY versus 2025 output of 741.1kt; company noted it could hit its longer-term 800,000-tonne annual target ahead of schedule if it reaches the top of the range.

Unchanged from 2025 guidance; 2025 actual output was a record 117,549 tonnes (near top of range), all from DRC operations. Production guidance is distinct from the much lower exportable volume allowed under the DRC quota (31,200 tonnes for CMOC in 2026).
Driven by KFM Phase II (adds ~100kt/yr, progressing smoothly per H1 2026 report) and TFM Phase III expansion.
New target following 2025 entry into gold via Lumina Gold/Cangrejos (Ecuador) and four Brazilian mines; Jefferies estimates gold could be >10% of group gross profit by 2030.
Declared alongside H1 2026 results reflecting the sharp YoY profit increase; total proposed interim distribution ~RMB2.03bn.

guidance.management_commentary: Management's FY2025 'Letter from the Board' frames strategy around a '622 model' (60% of cost advantage from resource endowment/M&A timing, 20% from mine planning/engineering, 20% from operational execution) and a newly articulated 'Copper-Gold Dual Core' strategy, citing the AI computing revolution and electrification as reshaping copper's industrial value, and gold's 'financial and risk-averse attributes' becoming more prominent amid geopolitical volatility. On cobalt export quotas, management said at the April 2026 AGM that maintaining normal (full) production remains the optimal strategy given TFM/KFM's high ore grade and low by-product costs, implying confidence in eventually monetizing constrained inventory as quotas evolve.

bull_case: World's largest cobalt producer benefiting disproportionately from the DRC's 2025-2027 export quota regime, which caps industry supply and has driven cobalt prices to multi-year highs while CMOC's low by-product cost structure lets it profit even with export volume constrained

Copper production growing double digits with a credible path to ~1 million tonnes group capacity by 2028 (KFM Phase II, TFM Phase III), positioning CMOC to benefit from structurally tightening global copper supply amid electrification and AI-driven power demand

Record, accelerating profitability: FY2025 net profit +50.3% YoY and H1 2026 net profit +86.3% YoY, with broad sell-side analyst support (Buy/Strong Buy ratings from BofA, Jefferies, Citigroup, Morgan Stanley)

New gold pillar (Lumina Gold/Cangrejos in Ecuador, four Brazilian mines) diversifies away from pure copper-cobalt cyclicality and gives management a credible, well-capitalized second growth vector with a long production runway
Proven contrarian M&A track record (TFM, KFM acquired near cycle lows) suggests management can continue to create value through disciplined, well-timed deal-making across commodities and geographies
bear_case: Profit is overwhelmingly concentrated in the DRC, a jurisdiction with a recent history of unilateral export bans, royalty disputes (the $800m Gécamines settlement), and discretionary quota administration (ARECOMS) that can abruptly reset CMOC's economics regardless of operational execution

Cobalt price strength is a policy artifact of DRC export restrictions rather than organic demand growth; any quota loosening, enforcement failure, or battery-chemistry shift away from cobalt could sharply reverse the 2025-2026 price rally

CMOC's own export allocation (31,200 tonnes in 2026) is far below its production capability (100,000-120,000 tonne guidance), meaning rising output does not translate one-for-one into sellable revenue, and inventory build-up/use-it-or-lose-it quota forfeiture rules add operational complexity

Heavy and rising capex (DRC capacity doubling, new gold-mine development in Ecuador/Brazil) alongside a 50%+ gearing ratio and a 35.6% YoY drop in FY2025 operating cash flow raises balance-sheet and execution risk if commodity prices soften

As a Chinese state/private-backed company dominating a critical mineral (cobalt) central to EV battery supply chains, CMOC faces latent geopolitical and Western supply-chain 'de-risking' policy risk that could affect market access, financing, or DRC-related exposures over time
